New TCS rate on foreign remittances explained

SYNTHETIC FIXTURE: fictional explainer used to test that the tax meaning of TCS is not treated as the company.

Tax Collected at Source (TCS) applies when individuals send money abroad under the Liberalised Remittance Scheme (LRS).

Under section 206C, the TCS rate on remittances above the threshold changes, and banks collect the tax at the time of the transfer.

TCS on foreign tour packages is also collected by the tour operator, and taxpayers can claim TCS credit when they file their income tax return.

A penalty may apply if the collector fails to deposit the amount, and the Income Tax Department can issue a notice for the shortfall.

Experts suggest planning large remittances carefully so that the TCS credit is reflected in Form 26AS before the return is filed.
